chunks: And by this chain, from Muhammad ibn Suleyman, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah and Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about wearing the fur and praying in it, so he said: 'Do not pray in it unless it is from what was purified (slaughtered).'
He said, I asked: 'Is the purified not that which is purified by the iron?' So he said: 'Yes, if it is from that whose flesh is edible.'

I said: 'And what is edible besides sheep?' He said: 'There is no problem with the squirrel, for it is an animal that does not eat flesh, and it is not of that which the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) prohibited; for he prohibited everything with a fang and a claw.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying in fur from animals other than sheep?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of praying in animal fur by linking it to the criteria of ritual slaughter (dhabihah) and edibility, specifically highlighting the squirrel as a permissible exception. The Imam distinguishes the squirrel from carnivorous predators by noting it is not among the 'dhi al-nab' (beasts of prey) explicitly prohibited, thereby refining the general rule against wearing fur from animals with fangs and claws.
